title: Explain-in-Plain-English and Prompt Problem lab tasks
summary: Engineering students complete 14 natural-language programming tasks across four weighted labs. They either describe supplied code so an LLM can reproduce it or infer a task from a visual specification and prompt an LLM to generate code, which is automatically tested.

sources.title: Integrating Natural Language Prompting Tasks in Introductory Programming Courses
sources.evidence_quote: Eight Explain in Plain English tasks were included in Labs 8 and 10, and six Prompt Problem tasks were included in Labs 9 and 12.

assessment.summary: Write natural-language prompts from code fragments or visual specifications, then use automated LLM generation and testing to evaluate whether the prompt captures the intended behavior.
student_actions: Read obfuscated C code and describe its purpose in plain English.
Infer computational tasks from visual input/output examples.
Inspect generated code and test outcomes.

student_role.description: Student prompts are sent to GPT-3.5, and the generated code is executed against instructor tests.

grading.method: The labs contribute to a 24% weekly-lab category; generated code is automatically judged with test cases.
grading.feedback: Students see generated code and test results.

reported_results: Final success rates were approximately 99% or higher across student difficulty groups.
Performance gaps on prompting tasks were smaller than gaps on invigilated programming exams.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.
